t: Which of the following expressions between critical constants and van der Waals constants is not correct?
s:
The critical constants of a real gas expressed in terms of van der Waals constants (a and b) are:
- Critical volume: V_c = 3b
- Critical pressure: p_c = a / (27b²)
- Critical temperature: T_c = 8a / (27Rb)

Combining these gives the critical compressibility relation:
p_c V_c = (a / 27b²) × 3b = a / (9b) = (3/8) R × [8a / (27Rb)] = (3/8) R T_c.

Thus:
- Option (A) correctly represents T_c.
- Option (C) correctly relates p_c, V_c, and T_c.
- Option (D) correctly gives V_c.
- Option (B) is incorrect because the true critical pressure is p_c = a / (27b²), not a(3b²).

Correct Answer: (B) p_c=a(3b²)

t: Three different gases X, Y, Z of molecular masses 32,64,71 were enclosed in a vessel at constant temperature till equilibrium is reached. Which of the following statements is/are true ?
s:
Free intermixing of gases results in uniform mixture.
Intermixing of the particles of substances on their own is called diffusion. A motion of the substances relative to one another throughout a definite region of space in which mixing is taking place. This relative motion is called diffusion. One of the properties of gases is that they mix with each other. When they do so, they become a solution-a homogeneous mixture. Each component of the mixture shares the same temperature and volume. (Remember that gases expand to fill the volume of their container; gases in a mixture do that as well.) .
o: Gas X will be at the top of the vessel
Gas Y will be at the top of the vessel
Gas X will be at the bottom and Z will be at the top
Gases will form a homogeneous mixture.
